ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a wooden board with mass $M=1\mathrm{kg}$ is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A small block with mass $m=2\mathrm{kg}$ (which can be treated as a point mass) moves onto the board from the far left end with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=3\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the small block and the board is $\mu=0.2$, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The magnitude and direction of the frictional force acting on the small block.
2. When the small block just rushes onto the wooden board, the magnitudes and directions of the accelerations of the small block and the wooden board, respectively.
3. To prevent the small block from sliding off the wooden board, what is the minimum length $L$ of the board?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$4\mathrm{N}$, direction to the left
$2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, direction to the left, $4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$
$0.75\mathrm{m}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a long wooden board is placed on horizontal ground, labeled with mass M; a small block is located near the leftmost end of the wooden board, labeled with mass m; beside the small block there is a velocity arrow v0, with direction pointing to the right, indicating that the small block slides onto the wooden board from the left end to the right relative to the originally stationary wooden board. The ground is drawn as a horizontal supporting surface. Reasoning: Take rightward as the positive direction. When the small block has just slid onto the wooden board, it moves rightward relative to the wooden board, so the kinetic friction force exerted by the wooden board on the small block hinders its relative motion, and the direction is leftward. The magnitude of the friction force is f=μmg=0.2×2×10=4 N. Apply Newton's second law to the small block: a_m=-f/m=-4/2=-2 m/s^2, so the magnitude of the small block's acceleration is 2 m/s^2, and the direction is leftward. The wooden board is subjected to the opposite friction force given to it by the small block, with direction rightward and magnitude also 4 N. The mass of the wooden board is M=1 kg, so a_M=f/M=4/1=4 m/s^2, with direction rightward. To require the minimum length of the wooden board, the sliding distance of the small block relative to the wooden board needs not to exceed the board length. The initial relative velocity is v_rel0=3 m/s, with direction rightward. The relative acceleration is a_rel=a_m-a_M=(-2)-4=-6 m/s^2, indicating that the relative velocity decreases with a magnitude of 6 m/s^2. When the relative velocity decreases to zero, the two reach common motion; the relative displacement before this is s_rel=v_rel0^2/(2×6)=3^2/12=0.75 m. Therefore, the minimum length to prevent the small block from sliding off the wooden board is L_min=0.75 m.
